images.author: Teemu008 from Palatine, Illinois
images.caption: 5016 North Kildare Avenue in the North Mayfair Bungalow Historic District in Chicago (1922).

facade.notes: the classic Chicago bungalow: a hip roof with a front gable dormer; the front is the enclosed sunroom, a ribbon of four windows with a planter box, and the entrance at the front corner reached by six concrete steps with urns on the cheek walls; limestone sill band, diamond brick inlays below; a clipped hedge and two columnar evergreens; a walk from the public sidewalk; cars parked at the curb

why.note: a full basement below the 42 in frost line: the main floor sits 4-5 ft up, 5-6 risers to the door
Chicago's bungalow belt: masonry required or favoured; brick bungalows built by the tens of thousands 1910-40
the Chicago 25-30 x 125 ft lot from the original plats; the house fills the width, leaving a walkway each side
the Chicago bungalow brings its porch indoors as a sunroom: usable in a Great Lakes winter
the side or corner entrance leaves the whole front for the sunroom's windows
